etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Via French pastiche, from Italian pasticcio (“pie, something blended”), from Vulgar Latin *pastīcius, from Late Latin pasta (“dough, pastry cake, paste”), from Ancient Greek παστά (pastá, “barley porridge”), from παστός (pastós, “sprinkled with salt”). Doublet of pasticcio.
senses: A work of art, drama, literature, music, or architecture that imitates the work of a previous artist, usually in a positive or neutral way.
A musical medley, typically quoting other works.
To create or compose in a mixture of styles.
